chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Zurara, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

"It is not appropriate that you pray the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf except near the Maqam (Station) of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). As for voluntary (prayers), then wherever you wish in the Mosque."
And the location of the Maqam is where it is at this moment; he narrated that.

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf

ai.seo_question: Where should one pray the two rak'ahs of Tawaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam, transmitted through the chain of Zurara, establishes a distinct juristic preference (istihbab) for performing the two rak'ahs of Tawaf immediately adjacent to the Maqam Ibrahim, while allowing flexibility for voluntary prayers elsewhere in the Haram. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on replicating the Prophet's and Imams' specific practices at the most sacred spot within the mosque, differentiating the obligatory ritual's preferred location from general supererogatory acts. The hadith underscores the sanctity of the Maqam as a focal point for worship, reinforcing the spiritual significance of proximity to Abraham's station during the Hajj rituals.
